items.text: Greer suffered an upper-body injury in Sunday's 6-3 win over Ottawa. items.headline: Greer scored two goals and added three hits in Tuesday's 6-5 overtime loss to the Canucks.
items.text: Greer has been productive with four goals and an assist over his last five games. He's mostly played on the fourth line lately, though the Ducks have mixed and matched their combinations regularly this season. Greer has six points, 20 shots on net, 27 hits, 28 PIM and an even plus-minus rating through 11 outings overall. That's a scoring pace that would show last year's 32-point campaign with the Panthers wasn't a fluke.

items.text: Head coach Lindy Ruff said that Benson's absence from practice was deemed a maintenance day, but the Sabres will see how he feels over the next few days before determining his status for Wednesday's game against Ottawa. The 21-year-old got banged up in the third period of Saturday's win over the Kings. Benson is expected to skate Tuesday morning and could join the team for practice, and a better idea of his availability for Wednesday could come into focus based on his participation level Tuesday.

items.headline: Benson logged two assists, including one on the power play, and added four shots on net and two blocked shots in Saturday's 3-2 win over the Kings.
items.text: Benson has two goals and five helpers during a four-game point streak. The 21-year-old forward is finding success on the top line, and he's also helped to spark Tage Thompson's offense during the Sabres' three-game winning streak. Benson is up to two goals, 11 helpers, 33 shots on net, 18 hits, 12 PIM, eight blocked shots and a plus-10 rating over 14 appearances this season.

items.headline: Benson scored a goal on three shots, dished two power-play assists, logged two hits, added two PIM and went plus-3 in Thursday's 7-6 win over the Ducks.
items.text: One of Benson's helpers came on the power play. The winger took some time to get going this season, but he's now scored in consecutive games, and he's gotten on the scoresheet in seven of his last eight outings. He's up to two goals, nine assists, 29 shots on net, 17 hits, 12 PIM and a plus-10 rating over 13 appearances. As long as he's playing in the top six and maintains a power-play role, Benson is poised to be a productive winger in fantasy, especially since he looks committed to upping his physical play this year.

items.headline: Benson scored an empty-net goal on five shots, added two PIM, logged two hits and went plus-2 in Tuesday's 2-0 win over the Sharks.
items.text: This was Benson's first goal of the season. The 21-year-old has added seven assists, 26 shots on net, 15 hits, 10 PIM and a plus-7 rating while seeing steady top-six minutes. Benson has plenty of talent, and his confidence should be up after seeing rubber meet twine to close out this contest. If he gets hot, there won't be many more chances for fantasy managers to buy low on him.

items.text: After initial reports regarding Capobianco's injury expected him to miss at least one week, he's likely going to miss four times that following his recent MRI. items.headline: Larkin (not injury related) will not play until he is traded away from the Red Wings, per Elliotte Friedman of Sportsnet.
items.text: After 818 regular-season outings across 12 seasons with the Red Wings, it appears that Larkin has suited up for Detroit for the last time. The 30-year-old center is expected to be traded in the near future after he recently made his 12-team trade list public. He initially put in a trade request in June, but ultimately remained with the Red Wings to start the new season, where he's compiled two goals, six points and 32 shots on net across 10 appearances. It remains to be seen which of the 12 teams on his trade list are pursuing the veteran center, but he can provide high-level two-way play up the center of the ice for the team that ultimately lands him. He's a strong player to stash in fantasy until his inevitable trade away from Motor City occurs.

items.headline: Larkin scored a goal on four shots in Monday's 4-3 shootout win over the Oilers.
items.text: Larkin hadn't scored since his season debut Oct. 6 versus the Senators, a span of eight games without a goal. He has two tallies, four assists, 32 shots on net and a plus-3 rating over 10 appearances. Larkin remains heavily involved in a top-six role and on the power play, and he'll look to stay productive to maintain his appeal as the Red Wings continue to search for a trade partner.

It remains to be seen how close he is to returning to the lineup, but when he does, he'll add major offensive firepower for the Kings, who currently rank 27th in the NHL with just 2.55 goals per game to start the season. He's a great player to stash on an IR spot in fantasy for the time being.

items.headline: Soderblom (upper body) was deemed day-to-day on Tuesday.
items.text: Soderblom is set to miss Tuesday's practice after popping up on Tuesday's injury report. The 25-year-old winger had seen heightened playing time as of late with Egor Chinakhov (lower body) and Evgeni Malkin (illness) sidelined. Soderblom was solid in those opportunities, posting an assist, five shots on net, a plus-1 rating, 14 hits and four blocked shots across six appearances. His status will be monitored ahead of the Penguins' next contest, which is Thursday's clash against the Mammoth.

items.headline: The Blues assigned Mailloux (hand) to AHL Springfield for a conditioning assignment Monday.
items.text: Mailloux underwent surgery to address a hand injury in late September, and general manager Alexander Steen said at the time that the 23-year-old defenseman would be re-evaluated in approximately eight weeks. While it's encouraging that Mailloux will join the Blues' minor-league affiliate as part of his recovery process, it's not yet clear when he'll be able to return to game action at the NHL level since he's still several weeks away from when he was initially scheduled to be re-evaluated.

items.headline: Parayko didn't practice Friday due to an upper-body injury but is considered probable for Saturday's game against the Red Wings, Lou Korac of NHL.com reports.
items.text: Head coach Jim Montgomery called Parayko's absence from practice Friday a maintenance day related to an upper-body issue that forced him to briefly exit Thursday's game against the Bruins. Montgomery said that Parayko will "probably" be able to play against Detroit, but the Blues will wait to see whether he's ready Saturday morning. If Parayko is unavailable, Montgomery said that the team feels comfortable inserting Quinton Burns into the lineup for his NHL debut.

items.headline: Parayko didn't participate in Friday's practice session after missing some time during Thursday's win over the Bruins due to an undisclosed injury, Lou Korac of NHL.com reports.
items.text: While Parayko ultimately finished Thursday's matchup, he was out for a portion of the first period due to an apparent injury. It's not yet clear whether his injury will impact his status for the Blues' upcoming four-game road trip, which begins Saturday in Detroit. If Parayko is forced to miss time, Quinton Burns is a candidate to see an increased role for St. Louis.

items.headline: Girgensons (lower body) won't play against Detroit on Tuesday, per Lightning reporter Gabby Shirley.
items.text: Girgensons will miss his third straight game, and it's unclear if he will be ready for Thursday's matchup against Chicago. If he doesn't play against the Blackhawks, Girgensons might be available for Tampa Bay's upcoming four-game road trip, which begins against Minnesota on Saturday. He has collected one goal, two points, 14 shots on net, 31 hits and nine blocked shots in 11 appearances this season.

items.headline: Mercer logged an assist and three shots on goal in Thursday's 6-4 loss to the Lightning.
items.text: The current headliner of the return for Connor Hellebuyck, Mercer's arrival in Winnipeg has gotten off to a slow start. The helper was his first point in three games with his new team. The 25-year-old has had some bad luck so far, coming up empty on 28 shots while adding five assists, nine hits, nine blocked shots and a minus-4 rating over 13 appearances between the Jets and the Devils. He's in a middle-six role with ice time in all situation, so he should be able to get his offense going soon, as long as he can adjust to his new teammates.
